p: Lakeside sits in West Thurrock, close to the M25 and the Dartford Crossing, so it's an easy one to reach from both sides of the Thames. That also means the roads around it can get very busy at weekends and in the run-up to Christmas, so leave a bit of slack in your journey to make sure you don't miss the safety briefing. Short nails, no dangly jewellery and empty pockets will make the climbing easier for everyone.

Once you've finished, it's worth knowing there's more to Thurrock than retail. Down in Grays itself, Grays Beach Riverside Park has a play area right on the Thames, where you can watch the ships heading in and out of the river. A short drive east, Tilbury Fort is an English Heritage site with impressive star-shaped defences that guarded the Thames for centuries.

For a nature fix, Chafford Gorges Nature Park is a surprising landscape of old chalk quarries turned into lakes, cliffs and woodland trails, with a visitor centre. Thurrock Thameside Nature Park, out towards Stanford-le-Hope, has views across the estuary and lots of birdlife. Either is a brilliant way to let little climbers stretch their legs in the fresh air after an indoor session.
